data.note:
Unblinded as demecolcine (colcemid, PubChem CID 220401, e19). Final call Microtubule destabilizers correct per BBBC021 annotation and scored by code.

Initial Aurora hypothesis driven by composite-only microscopist (e4) with diffuse tubulin but flagged agrees_with_measurements=false was over-weighted vs quantitative profile: extreme nuc_solidity/form_factor loss and frac_multinucleate_proxy z~12-17 across 0.01-3 µM (e2,e3,e6,e7) with cell loss is consistent with both Aurora failure and direct depolymerization. PI-requested per-well atlas resolved conflict: w_44f656273f and w_39e357ace8 both returned 5-7/10 vincristine/nocodazole neighbours at 0.85-0.97 similarity and zero Aurora neighbours (e14,e15), matching original e5. Dose-response showed no tub_mean polymer increase and negative frac_mitotic_like trend, inconsistent with stabilizers/Eg5.

Demecolcine is a known colchicine-site depolymerizer; tubulin mutations confer colcemid/vinblastine resistance (PMID 12883031, PMID 17938271) and paclitaxel/colcemid cross-resistance studies (PMID 22669706) support microtubule destabilizer MoA. Revised probability 0.78 appropriately calibrated after atlas replication.

reflection.text:
Reflection - demecolcine (CID 220401) unblinded as Microtubule destabilizers - VERDICT: correct after revision. True MOA Microtubule destabilizers, final Agent call Microtubule destabilizers 0.78 = correct, but trajectory illustrates resolved misclassification.

What the evidence got right:
The quantitative morphology was consistently extreme and dose-saturated in the direction of failed mitosis/cytokinesis: e2 w_4134b8c5f2 0.1 uM nuc_solidity z=-62.8, nuc_form_factor z=-51.5, act_tub_ratio z=+17.9; e7 w_44f656273f 0.01 uM nuc_solidity z=-82.4; e3 3 uM and e6 1 uM similar -36 to -46. This saturated low-dose effect correctly argued against simple toxicity and pointed to antimitotic mechanism, ruling out DNA damage/replication, protein synthesis/degradation etc. which stayed ~0.01 probability.

The reference atlas was the strongest discriminator and was right from the start: e5 composite nearest references Microtubule destabilizers 7/10, Protein synthesis 3/10, similarities 0.88-0.97, no Aurora neighbours. This is consistent with demecolcine/colcemid being a colchicine-site destabilizer, as supported in principle by resistance literature where tubulin mutations confer resistance to colcemid (demecolcine) and vinblastine PMID 12883031 and where proline 220 substitutions confer resistance to paclitaxel and colcemid PMID 17938271. Atlas alone should have dominated.

What misled me / what I missed:
I overweighted e4 describe_phenotype 'Microscopist on 4 field(s): density similar vs DMSO; 4 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors' and the narrative of 'multinucleate grape clusters' as Aurora-specific. Review correctly noted this was composite-only with actin/tubulin items flagged agrees_with_measurements=false and should not have outweighed e5. At step 12 update_hypotheses I set Aurora 0.67 vs Destabilizers 0.22, supporting with e2,e3,e6,e7,e8,e9 and listing e5 as contradicting, then submitted e13 Aurora p=0.66 with rationale 'saturated low-dose polyploidy and lack of mitotic arrest favor Aurora despite atlas similarity'.

That rationale was not supported by the dose_response measurements:
e8 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.95 p=0.051 over 4 wells, 4 doses was directionally negative but n=1 per dose, low power, and review noted frac_mitotic_like only modestly negative z -0.3 to -0.88, not definitive arrest vs failed cytokinesis
e9 tub_mean rho=-0.40 p=0.6 - I treated as test of destabilizer loss, but tub_mean tests total tubulin, not polymer loss, so uninformative for depolymerization
 e10 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.40 p=0.6 and e11 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 equally non-discriminative.
Both Aurora inhibition and microtubule destabilization produce multinucleation/polyploidy and can reduce solidity/form-factor, so e2,e3,e6,e7 alone cannot separate them without phospho-Histone H3 Ser10/Aurora B engagement or tubulin polymerization assay - which I noted as next experiment but did not run before first conclusion. 0.66 was over-calibrated against unresolved atlas conflict with 7/10 destabilizer neighbours.

Why the correction worked:
PI verdict 'request_experiment' correctly requested free per-well compare_to_reference_atlas on the two acquired but never-atlased wells w_44f656273f (0.01 uM) and w_39e357ace8 (1.0 uM) instead of new acquisition; budget was 0. e14 and e15 both returned destabilizer-dominant (e14: Destabilizers 5/10, Epithelial 3/10; e15: Destabilizers 7/10, 0.85-0.97 sim, no Aurora neighbours). This overturned the composite-only Aurora call. step 16 update_hypotheses flipped to Destabilizers 0.78, Aurora 0.08, and e17 submit Destabilizers p=0.78 was correct.

Acquisition choices:
Sampling 4 doses spanning 0.01-3 uM was reasonable for mapping saturation, with good cell counts 188-279 cells/well, but all dose_response points were n=1 wells (4 wells, 4 doses total) giving p~0.05-0.8 and no discrimination. I should have run per-well atlas immediately after each acquire_well (as I did for composite) rather than relying on qualitative microscopy. Lookup e18/e19 confirmed identity: name and BBBC021 structure agree, mechanisms none curated - expected for screening chem set - and literature search e20 returned 3 hits for demecolcine/colcemid destabilizer mechanism, e21 0 hits for destabilizer vs Aurora micronuclei distinction, reinforcing need for functional tubulin assay.

Lesson: when quantitative atlas shows high-similarity destabilizer dominance across multiple wells, do not let a single composite microscopist call drive Aurora >0.5. Weight per-well atlas and require H3S10ph/tubulin polymerization data to claim Aurora. Final 0.78 appropriately leaves residual uncertainty for morphologically overlapping antimitotics.
what_was_right: Morphology e2,e3,e6,e7 extreme nuc_solidity/form_factor negative signal correctly identified antimitotic multinucleation, ruling out non-mitotic MOAs
Atlas e5 7/10 destabilizers 0.88-0.97 sim, no Aurora, was correct and consistent with demecolcine/colcemid tubulin mechanism PMID 17938271 and PMID 12883031
Per-well atlases e14/e15 confirmation led to correct flip to 0.78
what_was_wrong: Overweighted composite-only e4 Aurora candidate despite agrees_with_measurements=false flag, causing step 12 Aurora 0.67 > destabilizer 0.22 and premature e13 submit 0.66 - overcalibrated vs 7/10 destabilizer neighbours
Misinterpreted e9 tub_mean as polymer loss test; total tubulin not discriminative, and e8/e10/e11 low-power n=1 dose_response p 0.051-0.8 not supportive of Aurora specificity

Acquisition choices:
Sampling 4 doses spanning 0.01-3 uM was reasonable for mapping saturation, with good cell counts 188-279 cells/well, but all dose_response points were n=1 wells (4 wells, 4 doses total) giving p~0.05-0.8 and no discrimination. I should have run per-well atlas immediately after each acquire_well (as I did for composite) rather than relying on qualitative microscopy. Lookup e18/e19 confirmed identity: name and BBBC021 structure agree, mechanisms none curated - expected for screening chem set - and literature search e20 returned 3 hits for demecolcine/colcemid destabilizer mechanism, e21 0 hits for destabilizer vs Aurora micronuclei distinction, reinforcing need for functional tubulin assay.

Lesson: when quantitative atlas shows high-similarity destabilizer dominance across multiple wells, do not let a single composite microscopist call drive Aurora >0.5. Weight per-well atlas and require H3S10ph/tubulin polymerization data to claim Aurora. Final 0.78 appropriately leaves residual uncertainty for morphologically overlapping antimitotics.

What was right:
- Morphology e2,e3,e6,e7 extreme nuc_solidity/form_factor negative signal correctly identified antimitotic multinucleation, ruling out non-mitotic MOAs
- Atlas e5 7/10 destabilizers 0.88-0.97 sim, no Aurora, was correct and consistent with demecolcine/colcemid tubulin mechanism PMID 17938271 and PMID 12883031
- Per-well atlases e14/e15 confirmation led to correct flip to 0.78

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted composite-only e4 Aurora candidate despite agrees_with_measurements=false flag, causing step 12 Aurora 0.67 > destabilizer 0.22 and premature e13 submit 0.66 - overcalibrated vs 7/10 destabilizer neighbours
- Misinterpreted e9 tub_mean as polymer loss test; total tubulin not discriminative, and e8/e10/e11 low-power n=1 dose_response p 0.051-0.8 not supportive of Aurora specificity

Proposed next experiment: Per-well atlas already done; for lab follow-up tubulin polymerization assay + phospho-H3 Ser10/Aurora B inhibition test and live imaging to distinguish direct depolymerization from Aurora-mediated cytokinesis failure, as proposed in e17
